title: Choose the visual world for VORXEN
question: The roll assigned The Robot Work Cell. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Robot Work Cell
options.lineage: Industrial robot cells: floor markings, safety placards, light curtains, homing sequences
options.thesis: VORXEN is a live, fenced robot cell you walk through; the machine is running and it notices you.
options.viewport: Boot runs a homing sequence (axes A1–A6 to 100%), the hazard shutter rises, and the Spline robot stands under an amber overhead light inside a painted floor square; VORXEN is set huge in Dune Rise across the floor, with zone placards at the corners and the light curtain tripping when your cursor enters.
options.risk: Can read blue-collar and industrial rather than premium AI if the amber spreads past the floor and placards, or if the lighting is flat.

raised.raise: Every system readout (stats, zone labels, modes) updates in fixed character cells, cascading one character at a time.
One vertical floor lane runs the full page with a live Y-axis position readout, and every section aligns to it.
Each zone gets exactly one dominant image or scene; nothing competes with it.

options.label: Self-Diagnostic Boot
options.lineage: Machine power-on self-test screens and diagnostic readouts
options.thesis: The whole site is VORXEN booting and running its own diagnostics, and you watch it wake up.
options.viewport: A POST log scrolls in, then collapses into the hero robot framed by calibration brackets and live sensor values.
options.risk: This is where most AI and robotics sites land: a cyan HUD on black that people have seen many times.

options.label: WebGL Shader Portal
options.lineage: Experiential studio portals (the sidewave.it / Awwwards WebGL lineage)
options.thesis: A breathing full-screen shader field is the ground, the robot emerges from it, and the UI is thin type floating over living pixels.
options.viewport: A loader counts to 100, then the shader field fills the screen with one oversized VORXEN word and tracked labels in the corners.
options.case: Wins on audience identification (studios recognise their own medium) but loses on product clarity: a robotics brand reads as a generic studio portal.
options.risk: Interchangeable with a hundred studio sites; the robot becomes incidental.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: VORXEN as a departure board of systems.
options.viewport: A board of rows listing modules and their states.
options.risk: A transit board that hides the robot.
options.case: Loses on both axes: no robot and no studio identification.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.viewport: A diver at the surface over an abyss.
options.kept: One vertical axis with a live position readout.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.viewport: Letters forming VORXEN as a storm.
options.kept: The footer wordmark behaves as physical matter.

options.label: Night-Market Sign River
options.risk: Warm street culture; wrong world for a machine.
options.kept: One shared order (the floor lane) running through very different zones.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark sci-fi AI landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A centred headline over the robot, a glowing CTA, and a row of feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AI landing page by design.
